h07.

Trace: `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar` → Echo handler → `Store` facade → SQL driver (three interchangeable driver implementations behind the same `store.Driver` interface — SQLite shown as representative).

- server.go — /bench/repo/server/server.go (registers `FileServerService` routes on the Echo server, lines 81-82)
- fileGroup.GET("/file/users/:identifier/avatar") — /bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go (route registration, line 124)
- serveUserAvatar — /bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go (HTTP handler, lines 168-210)
- getUserByUsername — /bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go (helper, lines 715-717)
- Store.GetUser — /bench/repo/store/user.go (checks `userCache`, then delegates, lines 148-169)
- Store.ListUsers — /bench/repo/store/user.go (delegates to driver, lines 136-146)
- driver.ListUsers — /bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user.go (builds and runs `SELECT ... FROM user WHERE ...`, lines 88-143; equivalent implementations exist in /bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user.go and /bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user.go)
- `avatar_url` column of the `user` table — the underlying SQLite/Postgres/MySQL database (stored data, read via `d.db.QueryContext`/`QueryRowContext` in the driver files above)

The handler then decodes the returned `user.AvatarURL` data URI (`parseDataURI`, same file, lines 737+) and streams it back as the image response.
